audit_notes: Model: same steady 1D roof conduction with linearised sol-air boundary as the other roof coatings; q = U*[alpha*I + h*dT - eps*R_net]/(U + h). Adjustments: clean SR 0.93 for closed glass cells with sub-micron BaSO4 in the walls is optimistic: closing the cells replaces part of the high-contrast air/particle interfaces by glass/particle interfaces (index ratio 1.64/1.5 instead of 1.64/1.0), and hollow-glass-microsphere roof coatings reach ~0.85-0.90; I set 0.92. Life-mean aged loss 0.05 assumes the sealed surface stays sealed; sand abrasion and thermal cycling will open a fraction of the surface cells, so I set 0.06 (aged SR 0.86). Emittance 0.93 plausible. Hand result: design q = 0.5*(0.14*300 + 150 - 0.93*85)/15.5 = 3.64 W/m2 vs baseline (SR 0.85 - 0.18 = 0.67, eps 0.90) 5.56 W/m2: -35 %. Dimensionless: h/U = 30; solar absorption number alpha*I/(h*dT) = 0.28 vs 0.66 baseline. Structural: closed-cell silicate glass foam layers (cellular glass) are strong in compression (~0.5-1 MPa) and inert; thin (~0.5 mm) layers on flexible roofs crack, so the coat suits concrete roofs and fibre-cement or ceramic facade panels (factory-fired). Simulation coefficient: U_eff = U*h/(U+h) = 0.484 W/m2K.
